scope: Suspected septic arthritis of a native joint, including the synovial-fluid steps that also look for crystals.

keyRecommendations.text: Aspirate synovial fluid as quickly as possible when septic arthritis of a native joint is suspected.
If fluid is limited, prioritise tests that include neutrophil percentage and crystals.
Except when the patient is septic, wait for the joint-fluid sample before empirical antibiotics so cultures are not falsely negative.

clinicalBottomLine: A hot native joint is aspirated immediately, the fluid is examined for cells, organisms, and crystals, and antibiotics wait for that sample unless the patient is septic.
notableCaveats: Reactive arthritis, seronegative inflammatory arthritis, and trauma are outside this septic-arthritis guideline.
